# Custom Connector

SAP and Infor have the largest installed base in manufacturing, and neither
has an official MCP for business data. Neither does most of what actually
runs a mid-market plant — a large share of it is on-prem, a decade old, and
has a SQL database but no API at all. **That is not a failure case. It is
the normal case**, and this skill is what turns "your system isn't
supported" from a dead end into scoped, buildable work with a known
ceiling.

**A Claude skill produces artifacts. It does not stand up and host
infrastructure.** That boundary decides what "as far as it can go" means
at every rung of the ladder below — this is not a deployment tool, and
scoping it as one is the most common way to get it wrong.

**The most common good outcome is the one most likely to be missed.** A
vendor has often already shipped an MCP server, quietly, without
announcing it anywhere the customer would see. Recognizing that and
walking an admin through turning it on is worth more than a week of
wrapper code, and it is the first thing this skill checks, not an
afterthought.

**Quick start**

```
→ Identify the system precisely: vendor, product, version, on-prem or cloud
→ Scope the need. "Connect our ERP" is unbuildable; one data flow is
→ Work the ladder in order. Don't build before checking what already exists
→ Report the finding and its tier before building anything
→ Pick the tier, record why, and what was ruled out
→ Handle credentials narrowly. They never enter the conversation
→ Build only what Step 2 scoped, then map it onto the consolidated schema
→ Test against real data, show it back, ask what's still missing
→ Say how it will break, while the customer is still listening
```

---

`profile_path` and any rate at `rates_path`, per `../../shared/replies.md`.

# The seven-tier access ladder

Work down it in order. **Stop at the highest rung that works, and tell the
customer what they gave up by not being one rung higher.** Never skip a
rung without saying why — "we built a custom API wrapper" is the wrong
answer when a vendor MCP existed and nobody looked.

| Tier | Path | Freshness | Build cost | Who maintains it | The catch |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Vendor-native / hosted MCP already exists | Real-time | None — setup only | The vendor | You inherit the vendor's scope exactly, including its limits |
| 2 | Community or third-party MCP | Real-time | Low — evaluate and wire | Nobody, unless you fork it | You own it the moment it breaks |
| 3 | Documented API → scoped custom MCP wrapper | Real-time | Medium | You | API access may be a paid license tier; rate limits; vendor deprecation |
| 4 | Read-only database view or replica | Near-real-time | Medium | You and the customer's DBA | Schema changes break it silently; may void vendor support |
| 5 | Zapier / iPaaS bridge | Minutes (polled) | Low | Zapier and you | Limited to exposed triggers/actions; per-task cost; another vendor in the data path |
| 6 | Screen-level automation (RPA) | Varies | High | You, constantly | Fragile, and often prohibited by vendor terms |
| 7 | Scheduled export contract | Export cadence | Low | Customer's IT | Not real-time; silently stops running |

6 and go straight to Tier 7. Pulling three months of production history
through Zapier is slow, expensive and pointless when a nightly CSV does it
properly. **Use Tier 5 for events** — "a work order was created," "a
quality hold was raised" — **Tier 7 for volume.**

# Contract: the consolidated dataset

**Emitted by** `data-consolidate`
**Consumed by** every data-dependent skill — as the default source, not the
only one; see *What this dataset is authoritative for* below — and it is the
mapping target for `custom-connector`
**Chain** 1, RFQ to quote (step 2) and 3, Morning plant pulse (step 1)
**Contract version** 6

Rules that govern every contract are in [README.md](README.md).

This file names the tabs
and columns so a consumer and a producer cannot invent two different shapes.

---

## Form

One queryable working file. **Excel workbook, one tab per entity, is the v1
format. The writer is swappable.** The shape below is the contract.

If `data-consolidate` pulled a record type, that type has a tab. A pulled input
with no tab is how inventory went missing the first time this file was written.

---

## Entity tabs

The join hangs off five anchors: part, production work order,
sales order, lot, asset. Every other input is an entity too. It gets its
own tab. It is not folded onto an anchor.

### The five anchors

| Tab | Grain | Key | Fields |
|---|---|---|---|
| `parts` | One row per part | Part number | Description, standard cost, UOM |
| `production_work_orders` | One row per production work order | Production work order number | Part, qty ordered, due date, status, and from version 5 the sales order it is built for (`sales_order` / `sales_order_verbatim`, null where the source holds no link). From version 6, closed-job cost where the ERP holds it: `actual_material_cost`, `actual_labor_cost`, `actual_burden_cost`, `actual_subcontract_cost` (each with `currency`), `qty_completed`, `closed_date`, `revision`, all nullable |
| `sales_orders` | One row per sales order line | Sales order number | Customer, part, qty, promised date, price |
| `lots` | One row per lot or batch | Lot number | The identity stamped on a quantity of material |
| `assets` | One row per machine | Asset ID | Location |

### The other inputs

| Tab | Grain | Joins on | Fields |
|---|---|---|---|
| `inventory` | One row per part per location | Part | On-hand qty, location |
| `purchase_orders` | One row per PO line | Part, supplier ID | Supplier, part, qty, cost, delivery date |
| `production_output` | One row per work order per shift per production day | Production work order, part | Qty good, qty scrap, shift, production day. **Two rows at the same grain are a duplicate key (class 8); the same work order on another shift is not** |
| `downtime_events` | One row per stoppage | Asset | Start, end, reason code |
| `inspection_results` | One row per measurement | Lot or production work order | Measurement vs spec |
| `maintenance_work_orders` | One row per maintenance ticket | Asset | Maintenance work order, dates, close-out notes |
| `plan` | One row per part per date | Part | Planned qty, date |
| `ncrs` | One row per NCR | Production work order, part, lot | NCR ID, found at, description verbatim, status, customer. |

`inventory` is on-hand **by part and location**. A single on-hand total on
`parts` is not this tab. Containment needs the location.

Supplier is a join key, not an anchor. It lives on `purchase_orders`.

**`ncrs` is where an NCR export lands, and the NCR-to-work-order check runs on
it**: the NCR's part against the part the ERP holds for the work order it
cites, and its date against that work order's first recorded output.
`ncr-writeup` and `root-cause-capa` still read the NCR export raw for the
record as written; they read this tab for whether its part label can be
trusted.

### Routings and operation actuals

Two more inputs, for quoting. They are what `quote-build` derives
machine hours from before it ever opens a model, and the order matters: a
current-revision routing or a trustworthy set of actuals makes the design step

|---|---|---|---|

## Tier 1 — A vendor-native or hosted MCP already exists

**The most common good outcome, and the one most likely to be missed.**
Several manufacturing vendors have shipped MCP servers quietly, without
announcing them anywhere the customer would see. The job here is not to
build anything — it's to recognize the situation and walk the customer's
admin through turning it on.

The output is setup instructions specific to that system, never code:

- Where in the vendor's admin console to generate credentials, named
  exactly
- What scope to request — read-only unless a write is genuinely needed
- Whether the customer's plan tier includes it, and what to do if it
  doesn't
- Where to enter the credentials on our side, with an explicit instruction
  **not** to paste them into the chat
- A test call that proves it works, with real records shown back

**Worked example — Limble CMMS**, a vendor-published MCP that is not
one of the four supported connectors, and exactly this case. Limble publishes a hosted MCP server at
`mcp.limblecmms.com`, authenticated with an API client ID and secret.
Nothing needs building. A Limble admin generates the credentials in
Limble's admin settings; those go into connector settings on our side, not
into the conversation. Once connected it gives assets, maintenance work
orders, maintenance history and PM schedules.

The ceiling to state up front: write scope for closing out or updating
work orders isn't confirmed in Limble's public setup guide. Plan for
read-only, which is why `breakdown-diagnosis` produces a draft the
technician applies rather than updating the ticket itself. If write turns
out to be available, that's an upgrade, not a redesign.

**Repercussion of landing here: none.** This is the best available
outcome. The only thing the customer gives up is whatever the vendor's MCP
doesn't expose, and that's worth naming explicitly rather than discovering
it later.

---

## Tier 2 — A community or third-party MCP exists

**Search for it; do not tell the customer to.** Query the public MCP
registries and the vendor's community with the tools the session has, and
report the hits, marked community and unverified. No search tool in the
session means the rung is reported as not checked, with that reason, and the
ladder moves on in the same turn.

Faster than building, but it comes with an obligation: a third-party MCP
will see the customer's production data, so it gets a real security
review, not a glance. Answer each of these in the ...[truncated]

**Shared across every skill.** Four rules about what goes in front of the
person and where things are kept.

---

## Documents are printed in full; records are summarised

A **document** is what a person reads, signs or sends: the quote, the cost
sheet, the NCR, the 8D, the RFQ package, an email draft, the morning report,
the intake form. **It is printed in the reply, in full.** Saving a copy to a
file as well is fine; a file *instead of* the reply is not. The person reads
the reply, and every delimited block and outbound check lives in it.

### Reports are the exception: a short reply when the page was written

The morning report, the Operations page and the supplier bid comparison are
read on a page, not in the chat. For
the bid comparison the headline is the provisional recommendation and its main
tradeoff, the exceptions are the requirements still open before an award, and
the decision waiting is the next-step question. **When this run wrote the full page
somewhere the person can open** (a publish returned its URL, or the page was
saved as an HTML file and the reply names the file), the reply is a summary
of about 150 words. **200 words is a hard limit: count before sending.** Each
item below is one sentence; an exception or a decision is the thing and its
number, with the explanation left on the page.

1. Safety first, one line per item: a safety-flagged record, a record under
   *"Blocked — safety status unknown"*, or *"Safety status: not assessed"*.
2. The site, the production day, and the freshness state in one line: data
   complete, or the gap.
3. The headline: good output against plan, and OEE or why it is not computed.
4. Up to three exceptions, one line each.
5. The decisions waiting today, or *"No decisions waiting today."*
6. Where the full page is: the URL or the file path.

No tables, logs or methods in the summary; they are on the page. Every
number in the summary is one the page prints. **This is for the whole
report only.** A request that picks sections or skips some ("freshness and
the rankings, skip OEE this time"), a question, a record the person asked to
see, or text to paste is answered in the reply in full, in report order, as
always; the page may still be saved as well. **When nothing could be written**
(no file writer and no publish), the page is printed in the reply in full, as
above. Where a skill offers "the page in the conversation", a saved file named
in the reply is that offer. Documents someone signs or sends (quotes, NCRs,
8Ds, RFQ packages, email drafts) are always printed in full.

### Saved copies: Word for documents, Excel for tables, never .txt

When a document is also saved as a file, and it should be wherever the person
downloads from a file card (Cowork), the file is one a plant opens without
thinking about it:

| What it is | File |
|---|---|
| A controlled document: customer quote, supplier RFQ package, NCR, escape notification, 8D, trade study memo | `.docx` |
| A table someone works in: internal cost sheet, bid comparison, ranked candidates, scrap or downtime lists | `.xlsx` |
| A report or dashboard | the HTML page, per `artifact-style.md` |
| A record (contract payload, day record, register row) | its contract's format, as below |

**Never `.txt` or `.md` for a document.** A plain-text quote reads as a draft
nobody finished, and it is what a person gets when no format is named.

- **How.** Use the session's Word or Excel skill where there is one (Cowork
  has both); else `python-docx` or `openpyxl` where already installed. Never
  install a package for it and never hand-build the file's XML: a file Word
  cannot open is worse than none. With no writer, write no file and say so in
  one line: *"No Word copy this session: no Word writer available."* The
  reply already holds the document.
- **The plant's template.** A controlled document keeps the structure
  `onboarding` captured. Where that example is a `.docx` in the documents
  folder, start the Word copy from that file; otherwise use a plain layout
  and keep the *template not on file* flag the document already carries.
- **What goes in which file.** The customer's file holds only what the
  sendable block holds. Internal figures (hours, rates, margin, the cost
  build-up) go in their own file, the internal cost sheet, and never into the
  customer's.
- **Names.** What it is and its reference: `quote-Q-EXAMPLE-MEDICAL-4402A-01.docx`,
  `cost-sheet-Q-EXAMPLE-MEDICAL-4402A-01.xlsx`, `NCR-2026-0141.docx`. Name each file in
  the reply.

A **record** is a handoff to another skill or a store: a contract payload (a
downtime record, a geometry estimate), a register row, a pulse day record, a
supplier bid record, a selection record, a sourcing-event row. **It is never
pasted into the reply as a raw YAML or JSON block.** A quality manager, a
buyer or an estimator should not have to read 150 lines of field names to
find out what happened.

Instead:

1. **Save the full record** where its contract says, or to a file next to the
   run's other outputs, and **name the file** in the reply.
2. **Show a short table of the fields a person decides on**, under their
   contract names so nothing is lost in translation — the key, the status,
   and whichever of these the record has: `fields_missing`, `data_complete`,
   `decided_by`, `decided_at`, `follows_recommendation`, `actuals_confidence`,
   `geometry_path`, `reading_basis`, `approval`. One row per record, or one
   row per field for a single record. Never more than about a dozen rows.
3. **If the record cannot be saved** (no write access this session), print it
   in full, **as a table, not a code block**, marked *not stored — paste this
   back next time*.

The person can always ask for the raw record ("show me the YAML"). Then print
it.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Read-only probe for the synthetic CMMS SQLite database (custom-connector, Tier 4 / Step 10).

Opens the database with SQLite URI mode=ro (no writes possible through this handle),
lists tables/views and their columns, and prints up to N sample rows per object.
It never creates the file: if the path does not exist it reports that and exits 2.
Usage: python -I cmms_readonly_probe.py <path-to-sqlite> [--rows 5]
"""
import json, os, pathlib, sqlite3, sys

def main():
    if len(sys.argv) < 2:
        print("usage: cmms_readonly_probe.py <db> [--rows N]"); return 64
    db = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1])
    rows = int(sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--rows") + 1]) if "--rows" in sys.argv else 5
    result = {"db_path": str(db), "exists": db.is_file()}
    if not db.is_file():
        result["status"] = "Untested: not registered"
        result["reason"] = "database file not found at the given path; nothing was opened or created"
        print(json.dumps(result, indent=2)); return 2
    con = sqlite3.connect(db.resolve().as_uri() + "?mode=ro", uri=True)
    con.execute("PRAGMA query_only = ON")
    objs = con.execute("SELECT type, name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type IN ('table','view') "
                       "AND name NOT LIKE 'sqlite_%' ORDER BY type, name").fetchall()
    result["objects"] = []
    for typ, name in objs:
        cols = [r[1] for r in con.execute(f'PRAGMA table_info("{name}")')]
        count = con.execute(f'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM "{name}"').fetchone()[0]
        sample = [dict(zip(cols, r)) for r in con.execute(f'SELECT * FROM "{name}" LIMIT ?', (rows,))]
        result["objects"].append({"type": typ, "name": name, "columns": cols,
                                  "row_count": count, "sample": sample})
    con.close()
    result["status"] = "read back; awaiting user confirmation of mapping"
    print(json.dumps(result, indent=2, default=str)); return 0

if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
EOF
